key_insight: A graph-based transpilation method lowers routing costs and scales to distributed superconducting quantum architectures with restricted connectivity.
engineering_relevance: Connectivity-aware mapping and fast routing make circuit compilation more practical for multi-QPU systems without assuming ideal hardware links.
method: Represent circuit interactions with a quantum interaction graph (QIG).
Use graph partitioning to map qubits across modules.
Apply a fast SABRE-inspired heuristic to route under connectivity constraints.
evidence_signal: On 48 qubits, the method reduced average aggregated costs by up to 24.72% and delivered >250× speed-ups on structured workloads versus DMapS; on 399-qubit IBM Flamingo, it maintained practical runtimes and cut structured routing costs by up to 51.96% versus DQC-adapted SABRE.
watch_item: Reported gains depend on workload, topology, and baseline; the abstract does not establish hardware-executed fidelity improvements.
paper_title: Scalable Transpilation for Overcoming Restricted Connectivity in Distributed Superconducting Quantum Architectures
